iPhone 18 Pro will launch in just a few weeks, and with major changes to this year's lineup, it's more likely than ever to become Apple's new default model.

With no standard iPhone 18, the iPhone 18 Pro will serve as Apple's default new model this year.

Apple has launched multiple new iPhones every year for years, and that will undoubtedly continue for years to come.

However, this fall's iPhone lineup is reportedly set for a major change.

Apple is dropping its usual 'standard iPhone' and 'Pro iPhone' options — meaning there's no iPhone 18.

Multiple reports indicate Apple is pushing the launch of the iPhone 18 and iPhone Air 2 to early 2027, leaving this fall's lineup to include only:

By pushing the iPhone 18 launch past its usual release window, the iPhone 18 Pro essentially becomes Apple's default new model this fall.

Those who want a more affordable device can still pick up last year's iPhone 17, iPhone 17e, or iPhone Air. But this fall and through the holiday season, neither Apple nor carrier promotions will feature 'iPhone 18' as the new default — the iPhone 18 Pro will take that role instead.

The iPhone Ultra is priced too high to be anything more than a niche option.

So for the average person who just wants 'the latest iPhone,' Apple will essentially be offering just two choices: the 18 Pro and the 18 Pro Max.

It's an interesting experiment that could make the iPhone 18 Pro the best-selling Pro model yet — but combined with the expected price hike, it's a gamble for Apple. Without an iPhone 18 to upgrade to, potential upgraders may hold onto their current iPhones longer.

Either way, we'll know in the coming months whether Apple's new plan pays off.

What do you think of Apple's iPhone lineup changes this year? Let us know in the comments.
